objective: B472: eliminate callback loss when several VS Code extension-host App Server mux processes run concurrently and overwrite one fixed sideband.sock/cap path.

root_cause.measured_topology: mux PIDs 703036, 896247, 924074 simultaneously alive during the B471 live canary, all bound the single fixed ~/.geoai/app_server_mux/sideband.sock + sideband.cap path
root_cause.beyond_b471_selector: B471 fixed the wrong-turn selector (unique-newest inProgress by startedAt); the still-open defect was topological -- every mux instance's start()/_bind_socket()/write_capability_token() unconditionally unlinked and rebound the SAME shared socket/cap path, so the newest process silently shadowed the origin thread owner's endpoint and every sideband call (regardless of which thread it targeted) reached only the newest mux's child App Server.

fix.per_instance_endpoint: AppServerMux now generates a random per-instance id (secrets.token_hex(4), same length as the legacy 'sideband' stem so AF_UNIX 108-byte deployments are unaffected) and binds sideband_dir/<id>.sock + <id>.cap. _bind_socket() never unlinks a pre-existing path -- on collision it regenerates a fresh id and retries (bounded, SIDEBAND_SOCKET_BIND_MAX_ATTEMPTS) so a live sibling instance's endpoint is never clobbered.
fix.atomic_registry: Each instance publishes sideband_dir/instances/<id>.json: instance_id, pid, pid_start_time (/proc/<pid>/stat field 22), socket_path, capability_path, owned_thread_ids. Written via the same hardened owner-only atomic-write helper as the capability token (0600, owner/uid checked, bounded size). Liveness resolution (_pid_is_live) requires BOTH pid alive AND matching start-time, so a later process that recycles a dead instance's pid is never mistaken for the original owner.
fix.owner_only_thread_tracking: AppServerMux._observe_extension_message records a thread id into owned_thread_ids ONLY when it observes the EXTENSION's own thread/resume, turn/start, or turn/steer request on the extension->child pump. dispatch_sideband() (the path every callback-bridge probe uses) writes straight to the child via _write_to_child and never passes through that observer, so a sideband thread/resume can never claim or steal ownership -- verified directly by driving the raw socket out-of-band.
fix.client_side_resolution: SidebandCallbackClient resolves find_owning_sideband_instances(sideband_dir, thread_id) before every call. Zero matches -> SidebandOwnerNotFoundError; more than one -> SidebandOwnerAmbiguousError. Both subclass BusyThreadError, so CallbackBridge._process_batch durably parks the whole batch via the existing non-blocking capped-backoff path and never touches the dead-letter hard-failure budget. Exactly one match -> the client addresses only that instance's socket/capability pair -- never a fan-out, never the newest.
fix.b471_preserved: select_steer_target, the unique-newest-inProgress-by-startedAt selector, and the mux's thread/resume projection (id/status/startedAt only) are unchanged.
